patch_resolves_note: The fixed source adds `BgpUpdateMessageLayer::isDataValid(data, dataLen)` to the UPDATE parse path. On the original malformed staged PoC the fixed binary reaches `update_guard` with `withdrawn_len_field_end = 64535` and rejects the fourth UPDATE before `update_after_restore` executes; on the adjacent `withdr_len_zero_boundary` mutation the same fixed binary reaches `update_after_restore` with `withdrawn_len_field_end = 23`, making the required root assertion genuine while preserving the downstream helper path only for an in-bounds withdrawn-routes field.

nodes.description: Source. The BGP parser materializes the attacker-controlled fourth TCP-payload segment as a mutable `BgpUpdateMessageLayer` after checking only the outer BGP header length floor and `messageType == 2`.

nodes.function: pcpp::BgpLayer::parseBgpLayer(unsigned char*, unsigned long, pcpp::Layer*, pcpp::Packet*)
nodes.description: Root cause. `parseBgpLayer()` instantiates an UPDATE layer without validating that the withdrawn-routes and path-attributes sublengths fit inside `dataLen`, so later mutators operate on an internally inconsistent 67-byte UPDATE.

nodes.function: pcpp::RawPacket::insertData(int, unsigned char const*, unsigned long)
nodes.description: ASan sink. `insertData()` calls `memmove()` with a negative size after `extendLayer()` computes an insertion point two bytes past the current raw-packet end.
The vulnerable NLRI setter still requests insertion at fixed offset 23 even though the current terminal UPDATE is only 21 bytes long.
Intermediate runtime event packet_extend materialized from verified transition assertion a_nlri_insert_offset_reaches_packet_extend.
